sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record mepu1234 (Mepuri), with reference records 581555, 546819, 143256
sources.note: No descriptive references; status extinct; comment: attested only by a wordlist in the rediscovered Natterer nachlass (Nowotny 1949; Kann 1989; Adelaar & Brijnen 2014), shown by Ramirez 2020: 359–360, 429–539 to be an independent Japurá-Colombia language. All three refs typed a wordlist or less / overview.

States the language is attested only by a wordlist collected by Natterer in 1831; explicitly contains no phonological information. Reference list is the source of the Archiv 63–64 and Jolkesky 2016 records above.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. [2024]. Arquivo 90: Arawak: Léxico Básico & Classificação (Classificação p. 1; Léxico Básico pp. 2–99, †Mepuri pp. 20–21 with 'JC (comparação)' column; Mapas pp. 100–105). In: 350 Línguas – Vocabulários Seletos (fauna, flora, léxico básico) de 350 línguas das Terras Baixas da América do Sul. Belém: Área de Linguística, COCHS, Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi (online databank presented by Denny Moore; PDF dated 2024-02-09, 105 pp.).
sources.note: Silent. The Mepuri section is a comparative basic-vocabulary table (c. 100 concepts + adverbs, a 3-line 'GRAMÁTICA' cell: nu-/-rnu 1sg, pi-/-phii 2sg, wa- 1pl, -ka progressive, ka- positive, kale 'onde?', kate 'de onde?') followed by fauna/flora/artefact words with cognate-set tags. Ramirez keeps acute accents and vowel length from Natterer on some forms (kámui 'sol', ʃéko 'dia', keehí 'lua', hitíke 'carne', no-kaphéni 'dedo', kajooiní 'Orion') but gives no phoneme line and no 'Notações de Natterer' note for Mepuri (he does for Parawana, Aroaqui, Wirina) and says nothing about what the accent…

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. [2024]. Arquivo 91: Arawak: Fauna-Flora (JC: Japurá-Colômbia) (Baniwa-Koripako pp. 1–26; †Kauixana 27–43; Yukuna, Kabiyari & †Resígaro 44–62; †Wainumá, †Mariaté & †Mepuri 63–65; †Yumana & †Passé 66–68). In: 350 Línguas – Vocabulários Seletos … Belém: Área de Linguística, COCHS, Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi (PDF dated 2024-02-09, 68 pp.).
sources.note: Silent. One page of Mepuri animal/plant/artefact words with cognate tags (haianna 'tatu grande', kauájanní 'veado', uatúʃu 'papagaio', vókoko 'pomba', makannaʃi 'milho' …); accents reproduced on some forms, no prose. Other languages in the same file get a phoneme line (Yukuna, Kabiyari, Resígaro '… + duração vocálica + sistema tonal', Kauixana 'o [ɔ], ts [ts ~ s]'); Mepuri gets none. No statement about Mepuri accent or tone anywhere in the file.

sources.citation: Jolkesky, Marcelo P. de V. 2016. Estudo arqueo-ecolinguístico das terras tropicais sul-americanas. PhD diss., Universidade de Brasília.
sources.note: Comparative/classificatory dissertation cited by Wikipedia for Mepuri's affiliation; not opened; would not contain a first-hand stress description.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333–352. doi:10.26512/rbla.v6i2.16285
sources.note: Nothing about Mepuri stress. Only mentions Meppuri on p. 336 as an Arawak language for which 'there seem to be no other sources than Natterer's word-lists'. Its remarks on Natterer's diacritics concern Bororo vowel quality (acute accent = central vowel, pp. 339–340) and possible tone in Cabixí (p. 338); no stress rule for any language.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Natterer's Linguistic Heritage. In Archiv Weltmuseum Wien 63–64. LIT.
sources.note: Companion overview of the Natterer collection; may discuss transcription conventions in more detail than the RBLA article; no stress description expected.

sources.note: Nothing on Mepuri: the passage only says that, per Szentmartonyi, 'outro grupo baré, os «Mepuris», vivia no Uneuixi, no Xiuara e no Marié'. No Mepuri forms, no phonology anywhere in the book.

sources.citation: Natterer, Johann. 1831 [MS]. 'S. Gabriel, 31 July 1831. Sprachproben eines Indianers von d[er] Nation Meppurí.. am Rio Curicuriari wohnhaft.' In: Wortlisten von Indianersprachen in Brasilien, 1817–1835. Universitätsbibliothek Basel, UBH T 2, section '[577] S. Gabrill [..] Sprachproben der Nation Meppari', scan pp. 577–584 (folios numbered 170–173). Digitized: e-manuscripta.ch, DOI 10.7891/e-manuscripta-128842 (online since 2022-03-02); mirrored at archive.org/details/natterer-wortlisten (Public Domain Mark, uploaded 2026-09-09).
sources.note: Primary data only: c. 150 German–Meppurí entries (kin terms, body parts, nature, animals, phrases, ethnonyms) in Natterer's German-based orthography. Most polysyllabic forms carry an acute accent on one vowel (e.g. Mutter minjó, Tochter notschó, Weib hinnátu, junger Mann tammáni, Bruder noláni, Schwester noitú, Hand nokáphi, Finger nokaphéni, Nagel nobátsche, Fleisch hilíke, Grossvater itú ~ itó 'klingt halb o halb u') plus macrons/breves for vowel length; the accent sits on final, penultimate or antepenultimate vowels in different words. There is no prose remark on pronunciation, accent or t…

sources.note: The scholarly edition of all 72 Natterer wordlists including Meppurí; the editors' introduction is the one place where Natterer's accent marks (e.g. the acute in 'Meppurí') might be interpreted as stress; even so it would be primary data, not a description.
